To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the use of probe substrates for testing GSI/OE chips with electrical and optical I/O interconnects is feasible and 2) probe substrate design and test strategies are critical to ensure that test time and cost are minimized.

(1) the use of a wafer-level testing approach with a probe substrate can reduce the test cost for GSI chips with OE components; (2) a test cost of less than $1 is achievable with the use of a test vehicle that includes a probe substrate and a GSI chip; and (3) the probe substrate approach is a promising solution for testing GSI chips with integrated OE components.

1) the proposed test methodology can test a large number of GSI chips with electrical and optical I/O interconnects, 2) a test time of 10-15s/chip is possible, 3) test costs are low, 4) the test methodology is scalable to future technologies, and 5) the test methodology can be used to perform parametric testing as well.

the development of a new technology, the so-called "Gigascale" (GSI) technology, which will enable the design and fabrication of large-scale integrated circuits with high-performance and high-density optoelectronic components.
the development of new technologies for the fabrication of large-area, flexible, and stretchable electronic devices for a wide range of potential applications.
the development of novel optical and electrical test structures and test methodologies for the wafer-level testing of gigascale chips with integrated optical I/O interconnects.
